- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3) and price is trending upward, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment turns negative after a rally, model fails to adjust downward — apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days following sentiment shift.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 3–8% to align with true mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.1 to -0.3), model tends to ignore them — apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion — if 10+ days of price above 73, reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to avoid “sentiment-driven overreach.”
